surrogate.title: Surrogate (published-profile)
surrogate.summary: Event knots (time, altitude, velocity) from official vehicle brochures/user manuals, interpolated every 5 s and laid along a constant-azimuth rhumb line from the pad (azimuth from NOTAM/hazard areas or from target inclination). One assumption splits horizontal motion from the published profile. Where a vehicle has no published profile, a family stand-in (LM-3B from the CALT manual) is used and labelled. ILLUSTRATIVE, not telemetry. Falcon 9 flights use SpaceX webcast telemetry (altitude and speed vs time) from a past F9 Block 5 Vandenberg launch as the family profile, timed to the mission's published SpaceX event timeline.

sim.title: First-principles 3DOF sim
sim.summary: Point-mass ascent simulator: rotating WGS-84 Earth with J2 gravity, US76 atmosphere drag, pressure-dependent thrust, staging/boosters/fairing/coasts; vertical rise, pitch kick, gravity turn then linear-tangent guidance optimized (Nelder-Mead) to reach the target orbit along the launch azimuth. Stage parameters from OSINT, each number sourced, derived or labelled an assumption. ILLUSTRATIVE, not telemetry. Long March vehicles run in timeline mode: published ignition/cutoff/separation times are hard events, burn rates from published thrust/Isp, and remaining free parameters fitted (bounded least squares) to the CALT manual LM-3B profile (altitude within 3.4 km at all events). Falcon 9 also runs in timeline mode: SpaceX's published MECO, stage-separation, SES-1, fairing and SECO-1 times are hard events, Block 5 masses and Merlin thrust/Isp from open sources, and steering and payload are fitted (bounded least squares) to the parking orbit implied by SpaceX's pre-launch state vector (CelesTrak SupGP), along an azimuth tuned so the orbit plane reaches the state vector's inclination (15-16: 155.87° for 70.007°; 15-18: 155.80° for 70.004°), inside the NAVAREA hazard corridor. Sims run through payload deploy: after final cutoff the stage coasts under the same WGS-84/J2/US76-drag model, with any published restart or kick-stage burn modelled from its published timing, to the provider's published deploy time (Starlink 15-16: SES-2/SECO-2 at T+53:01-53:03, deploy T+1:01:53; Starlink 15-18: SES-2/SECO-2 at T+53:07-53:08, deploy T+1:01:59; Kinetica-2 Y2 and LM-2C Xichang: CAS Space / CALT TYPICAL-sequence payload separation at T+514.7 s and T+545.7 s, not flight-specific). Where no deploy time is published (Electron HawkEye 360, Electron iQPS 9, USSF-432, LM-4B, LM-6A, LM-8A) the stage is propagated from insertion for two revolutions on the inferred insertion orbit (same J2 + drag model) and the file ends labelled 'inferred insertion orbit, +2 revs (deploy time unpublished)'. Ariane 64 Block 2 (VA271) also runs in timeline mode: ESA's booster separation, fairing jettison, core MECO, first Vinci cutoff and the 18 s second Vinci burn are hard events, and the file ends at the published deployment start.
